claims.claim_text_verbatim: We introduce a self-improvement loop for reasoning models based on the following observation: Even when the difficulty of a problem exceeds the model’s current solving abilities, an additionally supplied solution might enable the model to extract useful solution ideas in hindsight.
claims.claim_summary: Proposed self-improvement loop uses supplied solutions to extract useful hindsight ideas for hard problems

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We operationalize this by jointly training the same model to exhibit the following three capabilities: predicting solution ideas from problems alone, reverse-engineering ideas from problems and known solutions, and solving problems using provided ideas.
claims.claim_summary: The method jointly trains one model to predict, reverse-engineer, and execute solution ideas

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The loop alternates between reverse engineering such ideas from problems with supplied solutions and using these ideas as additional supervision for joint training of all three capabilities.
claims.claim_summary: Training alternates between generating hindsight ideas and using them to supervise all three capabilities

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We give a formal specification of our method and a concrete instantiation for interactive theorem proving in the Lean theorem prover; empirical evaluation remains future work.
claims.claim_summary: The paper provides a formal method specification and a concrete Lean interactive theorem proving instantiation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For a reasoning model, this presents a learning opportunity: even when a problem exceeds its current solving abilities, a supplied solution may enable it to extract a useful idea for solving that problem in hindsight.
claims.claim_summary: Supplied solutions enable reasoning models to extract useful solving ideas even for hard problems

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Such a reconstructed idea can then provide additional supervision for learning to develop a solution idea from the problem alone, before attempting to solve it.
claims.claim_summary: Reconstructed hindsight ideas provide supervision for predicting solution ideas directly from problem statements

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We operationalize this observation by jointly training a model on three tasks.
claims.claim_summary: The method operationalizes hindsight learning by jointly training a model across three tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: A hindsight component reverse engineers solution ideas from problems and known solutions.
claims.claim_summary: The hindsight component reverse-engineers solution ideas from given problems and reference solutions

claims.claim_text_verbatim: A foresight component predicts such ideas from problems alone.
claims.claim_summary: The foresight component predicts solution ideas directly from problem statements without reference solutions

claims.claim_text_verbatim: A solver component uses problems and provided ideas to construct solution candidates.
claims.claim_summary: The solver component constructs solution candidates given a problem statement and solution ideas

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All three components share a backbone network; for example, when their inputs and outputs can be represented as text, we may use a shared language model with role-specific prompt templates.
claims.claim_summary: All three system components share a unified underlying backbone network with role-specific prompts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The centerpiece of our method is an alternating training loop.
claims.claim_summary: The core feature of the proposed framework is an alternating iterative training loop

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In each iteration, the current hindsight component reconstructs ideas for a batch of problems with supplied solutions.
claims.claim_summary: Each iteration uses the updated hindsight component to reconstruct ideas for new problems

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We then jointly train all three components using the resulting data together with previously collected examples.
claims.claim_summary: All three components undergo joint training on newly generated and replayed training examples

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Concretely, given a problem x with solution y and reverse-engineered idea z, the foresight component is trained to predict z given x, the hindsight component is trained to predict z given x and y, and the solver component is trained to predict y given x and z.
claims.claim_summary: Training optimizes foresight to predict ideas, hindsight to reverse-engineer them, and solver to solve

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Thus, the capability responsible for producing additional supervision is itself an explicit training target.
claims.claim_summary: The hindsight component generating additional supervision is explicitly trained alongside the other components

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We express solution ideas at several levels of detail, forming a hierarchy from overarching strategies to detailed plans.
claims.claim_summary: Solution ideas are structured hierarchically, spanning overarching strategies down to detailed plans

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Hindsight starts from a known solution, reconstructs a detailed plan, and compresses it into coarser ideas.
claims.claim_summary: Hindsight reconstructs detailed plans from solutions and compresses them into broader strategy ideas

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Foresight proceeds in the opposite direction, predicting a coarse idea from the problem and progressively refining it.
claims.claim_summary: Foresight predicts broad solution ideas from problems and progressively refines them into details

claims.claim_text_verbatim: During inference, the solver uses the hierarchy predicted by the foresight component to construct a solution candidate.
claims.claim_summary: At inference time, the solver generates candidate solutions using foresight-predicted idea hierarchies

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The ideas reverse-engineered by the hindsight component are intended to provide guidance that could plausibly be followed from the problem alone, rather than merely describe the supplied solution or reflect hindsight bias.
claims.claim_summary: Hindsight-derived ideas are designed to offer forward-usable guidance while avoiding hindsight bias

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We provide an optional refinement of our method which accomplishes this in the case of verifiable problem domains, i.e., when proposed solution candidates can be procedurally verified: For each problem and reference solution, we generate several candidate hierarchies in hindsight.
claims.claim_summary: In verifiable domains, the method generates multiple hindsight hierarchy candidates per problem

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The solver then repeatedly attempts the problem using each hierarchy, while the reference solution is withheld.
claims.claim_summary: The solver evaluates candidate hierarchies by attempting problems without access to reference solutions

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We then compute a score for each hierarchy, based on its success ratio under the repeated solver attempts and, optionally, domain-specific quantities.
claims.claim_summary: Hierarchies are scored based on solver success ratios and domain-specific evaluation metrics

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We retain the highest-scoring hierarchy and an associated valid solution for training, provided the score meets an acceptance threshold.
claims.claim_summary: Only top-scoring hierarchies and valid solutions meeting an acceptance threshold are kept for training

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We provide a formal specification of our method for a general problem setting, together with the optional refinement for verifiable problem domains.
claims.claim_summary: The paper formalizes the general method along with an optional verifiable domain refinement

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We also give a concrete instantiation for interactive theorem proving in the Lean theorem prover [2], where natural language proof ideas guide tactic generation during proof search.
claims.claim_summary: The approach is concretely instantiated for Lean, using natural language ideas to guide tactics

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our method makes retrospective generation of hierarchies (i.e., rationales at several levels of detail) an explicitly trained task.
claims.claim_summary: Retrospective multi-level hierarchy generation is formulated as an explicitly trained capability

claims.claim_text_verbatim: A shared backbone is jointly trained on three tasks: reverse engineering hierarchies from problems and reference solutions; predicting such hierarchies from problems alone; and solving problems using these hierarchies.
claims.claim_summary: A single backbone is jointly optimized across reverse-engineering, predicting, and solving with hierarchies

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Each retained training triple supervises all three tasks.
claims.claim_summary: Every accepted training triple simultaneously provides supervisory signals for all three tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The training loop alternates between generating training triples by reverse engineering hierarchies and jointly training on the above three tasks.
claims.claim_summary: The method alternates between generating retrospective triples and jointly fine-tuning on them

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Consequently, subsequent retrospective hierarchy generation uses the updated model, with the aim of improving the hierarchies available for further training.
claims.claim_summary: Retrospective generation uses updated models to progressively improve generated training hierarchies

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This differs from the forward generation of thoughts and tactics in Lean-STaR’s expert iterations, and from DeepInsight’s retrospective rationale generation using a teacher model: our loop repeatedly performs retrospective hierarchy generation with the same backbone that learns to predict and use the resulting hierarchies.
claims.claim_summary: Unlike Lean-STaR and DeepInsight, this loop repeatedly generates retrospective hierarchies using its own backbone

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Finally, in verifiable problem domains, we additionally assess the reverse-engineered hierarchies through separate solving attempts, in which the model receives the problem and hierarchy while the reference solution is withheld.
claims.claim_summary: In verifiable domains, hindsight hierarchies are validated through separate solution attempts without references

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We then select training triples based on this assessment, introducing an additional training signal through data selection, in the spirit of expert iteration [1].
claims.claim_summary: Data selection based on solver performance introduces an expert-iteration training signal

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our central hypothesis is that reverse engineering the idea underlying a known solution is, in general, easier than discovering it from the problem alone.
claims.claim_summary: The core hypothesis holds that reverse-engineering solution ideas is easier than solving from scratch
